pool.text: The Coptic Catholic minority established the Eparchy of Luqsor alias Thebes on November 26.
The Eparchy lost territory to establish the Eparchy of Assiut on August 10.
The Eparchy lost territory to establish Sohag on September 14.
Luxor became the only city offering hot air balloon rides in Egypt.
The local economy was hit by the Luxor massacre where 64 people died.
Excavation started around this year for a controversial tourism development plan in Luxor.
Nineteen tourists died when a hot air balloon crashed near Luxor on February 26.
The Egyptian Ministry of Antiquities announced the discovery of the shrine of Osiris.
A well-preserved mummy of a woman inside an unopened coffin was found on November 24.
Zahi Hawass revealed an ancient industrial area used to manufacture decorative artefacts for royal tombs.
Thirty well-preserved wooden coffins were unearthed in front of the Mortuary Temple of Hatshepsut.
The Egyptian Government announced the discovery of a previously unopened coffin dated back to the 18th dynasty.
Egyptian archaeologists led by Zahi Hawass found Aten, a lost golden city near Luxor.
Luxor had a population of 284,952 and served as the capital of the Luxor Governorate.
A team announced the discovery of the tomb of Thutmose II near Luxor.
Egyptian archaeologists uncovered three ancient New Kingdom tombs at the Dra Abu el-Naga necropolis.
An archaeological mission identified the owner of Kampp 23 as the mayor of Thebes Amun Mes.
